::: {#exr-lamb-speak-rug}
The hill() function is used extensively to represent the relative probabilies of random outcomes whose values tend to cluster about a specified mean. (hill() is used so extensively that it's often called the "normal distribution.")

For each of these depictions of the normal distribution, figure out what input scaling was used, that is, what are the values of $a$ and $q_0$ in the expression hill($a (\text{size} - q_0)$).

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| layout-ncol: 2
doplot <- function(a, q0, dom, ...) {
  f <- function(size) dnorm(size, q0, a)
  slice_plot(f(size) ~ size, dom, npts = 500) |>
  gf_hline(yintercept = ~ 0, color = "blue", alpha = 0.5) |>
  gf_labs(x = "Size of object (mm)", y = "Relative probability")
}
doplot(2, 5, domain(size=0:12))
doplot(0.5, 2.5, domain(size=0:4))
doplot(0.2, 1, domain(size=0:1.5))
doplot(7, 12, domain(size=0:40))
```

:::
